topicLabel: T2.1 · Uses Recommended Development Tools and Workflows
title: T2.1: Uses Recommended Development Tools and Workflows
description: Test your knowledge of InterSystems IRIS development tools, Visual Studio Code integration, debugging, Docker Compose, and background execution strategies

questions.question: Which of the following should be considered when deciding whether to use client-side or server-side editing for InterSystems IRIS code development in Visual Studio (VS) Code?

options.text: The use of the InterSystems Server Manager extension to authenticate connections to the IRIS server
Whether developers need to work with source files stored locally on their workstations or directly on the IRIS server
The programming language being used (ObjectScript vs. Python)
The size of the IRIS database

questions.explanation: Client-side editing involves working with source files stored locally on the developer's workstation and pushing them to the IRIS server, while server-side editing works directly with code stored on the IRIS server. This choice impacts source control integration, collaboration workflows, and development environment setup. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_INTRO

questions.question: Which VS Code extensions are essential for InterSystems IRIS development?

options.text: InterSystems ObjectScript
InterSystems Server Manager
Docker
Python
JavaScript Debugger

questions.explanation: The InterSystems ObjectScript extension provides language support, debugging, and code editing features for ObjectScript. The InterSystems Server Manager extension manages connections to IRIS servers and authentication. While Docker and Python extensions may be useful for containerized or Python development, they are not essential for basic IRIS ObjectScript development. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_INTRO

questions.question: You are configuring a VS Code workspace for server-side editing. Which setting in the objectscript.conn configuration enables direct editing of code on the IRIS server?

options.text: "server": true
"active": true
"serverSideEditing": true
"ns": "USER"

questions.explanation: The 'active' setting in objectscript.conn determines which server connection is currently active. For server-side editing, you configure the connection with host, port, username, password, and namespace, then set 'active': true to enable editing code directly on the IRIS server without local files. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO

questions.question: A developer wants to configure VS Code to connect to an IRIS instance running on a remote server at 192.168.1.100 on port 52773 in the MYAPP namespace. Which configuration is correct?

options.text: {"host": "192.168.1.100", "port": 52773, "username": "_SYSTEM", "password": "SYS", "ns": "MYAPP", "active": true}
{"server": "192.168.1.100:52773", "namespace": "MYAPP", "active": true}
{"endpoint": "192.168.1.100", "port": "52773", "database": "MYAPP"}

questions.explanation: The correct configuration requires host (IP or hostname), port (web server port, typically 52773), username, password, ns (namespace), and active (true to make this connection active). The host should be just the IP/hostname without protocol or port. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO

questions.question: When using the VS Code debugger with InterSystems IRIS, what is the purpose of setting a breakpoint in your ObjectScript code?

options.text: To permanently stop execution at that line until the code is recompiled
To pause execution at that line, allowing you to inspect variable values and step through code
To log a message to the console when that line is reached
To mark the line for code coverage analysis

questions.explanation: Breakpoints pause code execution at a specific line, allowing developers to inspect the current state of variables, evaluate expressions, and step through code line-by-line. This is essential for debugging complex logic and understanding program flow. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_DEBUG

questions.question: Which debugging features are available when using the VS Code debugger with InterSystems IRIS?

options.text: Setting breakpoints on ObjectScript code lines
Viewing and modifying local variable values during execution
Stepping over, into, and out of method calls
Time-travel debugging to rewind execution
Watch expressions to monitor specific variables or expressions

questions.explanation: VS Code debugging with IRIS supports breakpoints, variable inspection and modification, step controls (over/into/out), and watch expressions. Time-travel debugging (rewinding execution) is not currently supported. These features enable effective troubleshooting of ObjectScript applications. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_DEBUG

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the launch.json file in a VS Code workspace for IRIS development?

options.text: To define the IRIS server connection parameters
To configure debugging launch configurations and attach settings
To specify which files should be synchronized with the IRIS server
To list all ObjectScript classes in the project

questions.explanation: The launch.json file in .vscode/ directory defines debugging configurations, including how to launch or attach the debugger to IRIS processes. It specifies the program to debug, request type (launch/attach), and other debugging parameters. Server connections are configured separately in settings.json. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_DEBUG

questions.question:
A Docker Compose file for IRIS development includes the following service definition:

```yaml
services:
  iris:
    image: intersystemsdc/iris-community:latest
    ports:
      - "52773:52773"
      - "1972:1972"
```

What do the port mappings "52773:52773" and "1972:1972" represent?

options.text: The first number is the container port, the second is the host port
The first number is the host port, the second is the container port
Both numbers must always be identical for IRIS to function
The first is the HTTP port, the second is the HTTPS port

questions.explanation: In Docker Compose port mappings, the format is 'host:container'. Port 52773 is the IRIS web server/management portal (HTTP), and 1972 is the superserver port for client connections. The host and container ports don't need to match, but using the same values simplifies configuration. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: Which Docker Compose file components are commonly used for InterSystems IRIS development environments?

options.text: volumes: to persist database files and share source code
environment: to set IRIS configuration variables like passwords
networks: to enable communication between IRIS and other services
build: to compile IRIS from source code
command: to customize IRIS startup parameters

questions.explanation: Docker Compose for IRIS development typically uses volumes (for persistence and code sharing), environment variables (for configuration like ISC_DATA_DIRECTORY and passwords), networks (for multi-container communication), and command overrides (for startup customization). IRIS is not compiled from source; pre-built images are used. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: In a Docker Compose file for IRIS, you want to mount a local directory containing ObjectScript source code into the container. Which configuration accomplishes this?

options.text:
volumes:
  - ./src:/home/irisowner/src

mount:
  - type=bind,source=./src,target=/home/irisowner/src

copy:
  - ./src:/home/irisowner/src

shared:
  - ./src:/home/irisowner/src

questions.explanation: The 'volumes' section in Docker Compose uses the format 'host_path:container_path' to mount local directories into containers. This enables sharing source code between your workstation and the IRIS container for development workflows. The 'mount' syntax shown is Docker CLI format, not Compose. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: You need to set the initial IRIS _SYSTEM account password in a Docker Compose file. Which environment variable should be used?

options.text: IRIS_SYSTEM_PASSWORD
ISC_SYSTEM_PASSWORD
SYSTEM_PASSWORD
ISC_CPF_MERGE_FILE

questions.explanation: ISC_SYSTEM_PASSWORD environment variable sets the _SYSTEM account password during IRIS container initialization. Other common variables include ISC_DATA_DIRECTORY for data location. ISC_CPF_MERGE_FILE is for configuration file merging, not password setting. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: Which InterSystems tool provides a web-based interface for developing and managing InterSystems IRIS applications?

options.text: Studio
Management Portal
Atelier
System Console

questions.explanation: The Management Portal is the primary web-based interface for IRIS administration and development. It provides access to system configuration, class editing, SQL query tools, monitoring, and more. Studio is a legacy Windows IDE (deprecated), Atelier was an Eclipse-based IDE (also deprecated), and VS Code is now the recommended development environment. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSA

questions.question: Which development tools and features are available in the InterSystems IRIS Management Portal?

options.text: SQL query execution and routine viewer
SQL query execution and schema browser
System configuration and monitoring
Server-side source control hooks
REST API testing interface

questions.explanation: The Management Portal includes SQL query tools, routine viewing capabilities, comprehensive system management, and configuration for server-side source control hooks. Note that the Portal does NOT include a full class editor for ObjectScript development - that functionality is provided by IDE tools like VS Code or the legacy Studio. REST API testing is typically done with external tools like Postman or curl. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSA

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using the Terminal in the Management Portal?

options.text: It provides faster performance than local terminal emulators
It allows executing ObjectScript commands and routines directly in the IRIS environment
It replaces the need for SSH access to the server
It automatically logs all commands for audit purposes

questions.explanation: The Management Portal Terminal provides direct access to the ObjectScript command line within the IRIS environment, allowing developers to execute commands, call routines, inspect globals, and perform interactive debugging. It's a web-based interface to the IRIS process, not a system shell. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GSA

questions.question: Which InterSystems IRIS utility class provides methods for generating comprehensive code documentation?

options.text: %Compiler.DocGen
%Studio.SourceControl.Documentation
%Library.Documentation
%SYSTEM.OBJ.Documentation

questions.explanation: %Compiler.DocGen provides methods to generate HTML documentation from ObjectScript classes, including class descriptions, method signatures, parameters, and embedded documentation. This enables automated documentation generation as part of the development workflow. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/iris20253/csp/documatic/%25CSP.Documatic.cls?PAGE=CLASS&LIBRARY=%25SYS&CLASSNAME=%25Compiler.DocGen

questions.question: Which documentation approaches are recommended for InterSystems IRIS applications?

options.text: Inline comments in ObjectScript code using //
Class descriptions using the Description parameter
Method documentation using /// comments
Separate README files in the repository
Documenting parameter purposes and default values

questions.explanation: Comprehensive documentation includes inline comments (//), class-level Description parameters, method documentation with /// comments (which appear in generated docs), README files for project overview, and parameter documentation. This multi-layered approach ensures code maintainability and knowledge transfer. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_classes

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for adding documentation comments to a class method that will be included in generated documentation?

options.text:
// This method calculates the total
ClassMethod CalculateTotal() As %Numeric

/* This method calculates the total */
ClassMethod CalculateTotal() As %Numeric

/// This method calculates the total
ClassMethod CalculateTotal() As %Numeric

# This method calculates the total
ClassMethod CalculateTotal() As %Numeric

questions.explanation: Triple-slash comments (///) are special documentation comments that are extracted by documentation generation tools like %Compiler.DocGen. Regular comments (//) are not included in generated documentation. This syntax is similar to XML documentation comments in C# or JavaDoc in Java. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_classes

questions.question: Which ObjectScript command is used to execute code in a background process?

options.text: SPAWN
JOB
FORK
BACKGROUND

questions.explanation: The JOB command spawns a new background process that runs independently of the calling process. This is essential for long-running tasks, parallel processing, or operations that should not block the user interface. The syntax is: JOB routine^package(parameters). Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: You need to run a long-running data import process in the background. Which code correctly implements this using the JOB command?

options.text: JOB ImportData^DataLoader(filename)

SET job = ##class(DataLoader).ImportData(filename)
DO job.Start()
DO &JOB ImportData^DataLoader(filename)
SPAWN ImportData^DataLoader(filename

questions.explanation: The JOB command syntax is: JOB entrypoint^routine(parameters). This starts a new process that executes the specified routine or method independently. The job runs asynchronously, and control returns immediately to the calling code. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: What considerations should be taken into account when using the JOB command for background execution?

options.text: The background job runs in a separate process with its own memory space
You must use globals or other persistent storage for inter-process communication
The background job automatically shares all local variables with the parent process
You can specify job parameters like namespace and process priority
Error handling in the background job should be implemented within the job itself

questions.explanation: Background jobs run in separate processes with isolated memory, so local variables are NOT shared. Communication requires globals, files, or other persistent mechanisms. Job parameters can control namespace, timeout, and other settings. Each job must implement its own error handling as exceptions don't propagate to the parent. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: Which special variable is used to check if a JOB command successfully started a background process?

options.text: $JOB
$TEST
$SYSTEM
$ZJOB

questions.explanation: After a JOB command, the $TEST special variable is set to 1 (true) if the job was successfully started, or 0 (false) if it failed. This allows proper error handling: JOB routine^package IF '$TEST WRITE "Job failed to start". Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: A background job needs to update a global to report its progress. Which code pattern correctly implements this?

options.text: In the job: SET ^JobStatus($JOB) = "Processing record " _ recordNum
In the job: RETURN "Processing record " _ recordNum
In the job: WRITE "Processing record " _ recordNum (output automatically shared)
In the job: SET $JOB.Status = "Processing record " _ recordNum

questions.explanation: Background jobs must use persistent storage like globals to communicate state back to the parent process or other processes. Setting a global (^JobStatus) with $JOB as the subscript is the correct approach - $JOB contains the current process ID. RETURN only returns to the local job context, WRITE output is not shared, and $JOB.Status is not a valid syntax. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: You want to run a background job in a specific namespace different from the current one. Which JOB command parameter accomplishes this?

options.text: JOB routine^package(params):NAMESPACE="MYAPP"
JOB routine^package(params):NS="MYAPP"
JOB routine^package(params):(:NAMESPACE="MYAPP")
JOB routine^package(params):(::NAMESPACE="MYAPP")

questions.explanation: The JOB command uses the syntax: JOB entrypoint:(timeout:parameters) where parameters can include NAMESPACE="name". The format is JOB routine:(:(NAMESPACE="MYAPP")). The first colon is timeout, second colon precedes parameters. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: Scenario: Your team is developing a multi-container IRIS application with a web frontend, IRIS database, and Mosquitto MQTT broker for messaging. How should the Docker Compose file be structured?

options.text: Use a single service with IRIS and install Mosquitto inside the IRIS container
Define separate services for each component and use networks to connect them
Use only IRIS since external message brokers are not recommended with IRIS
Create separate docker-compose.yml files for each service

questions.explanation: Docker Compose best practices recommend defining separate services for each component (iris, web, mosquitto) in a single docker-compose.yml file. Use the 'networks' section to enable inter-container communication. This follows microservices principles and makes each component independently scalable and maintainable. Note: Redis is not recommended with IRIS as IRIS has its own built-in caching mechanisms. External services like MQTT brokers (Mosquitto), Kafka, or other messaging systems are appropriate integration targets. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: Which VS Code workspace settings are specific to InterSystems IRIS development?

options.text: objectscript.conn - defines server connections
objectscript.export - configures code export settings
objectscript.format - controls code formatting preferences
intersystems.language.diagnostics - enables real-time syntax checking
git.enableSmartCommit - enables Git integration

questions.explanation: IRIS-specific settings include objectscript.conn (server connections), objectscript.export (export configuration), and objectscript.format (formatting). The diagnostics setting mentioned is not a standard IRIS extension setting, and git.enableSmartCommit is a general VS Code Git setting, not IRIS-specific. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO

questions.question: When debugging a web service request in VS Code, which launch configuration type should be used to attach the debugger to an already-running IRIS process?

options.text: {"type": "objectscript", "request": "launch"}
{"type": "objectscript", "request": "attach"}
{"type": "iris", "request": "debug"}
{"type": "web", "request": "attach"}

questions.explanation: For debugging already-running processes like web service requests, use 'request': 'attach' in the launch.json configuration. This attaches the debugger to an active IRIS process when it hits a breakpoint. 'launch' is for starting a new debug session from the beginning. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO_DEBUG

questions.question: You need to pass parameters to a background job for processing. Which syntax correctly passes multiple parameters?

options.text: JOB ProcessData^DataHandler(param1, param2, param3)
JOB ProcessData^DataHandler:PARAMS(param1, param2, param3)
JOB ProcessData^DataHandler WITH param1, param2, param3
JOB ProcessData^DataHandler[param1, param2, param3]

questions.explanation: Parameters are passed to background jobs using standard parameter syntax in parentheses after the routine name: JOB routine(param1, param2, param3). These parameters are passed by value to the background process. The parameters must match the routine's parameter list. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob

questions.question: Scenario: You're setting up a development environment for a team using VS Code with both client-side and server-side editing workflows. What configuration considerations are important?

options.text: Configure .vscode/settings.json with separate connection profiles for different servers
Use workspace-level settings to share team configurations while keeping credentials in user settings
Set up .gitignore to exclude sensitive connection information
All developers must use identical VS Code versions
Configure isfs:// URI scheme for server-side file browsing

questions.explanation: Best practices include: multiple connection profiles for different environments, workspace settings for shared configuration (with credentials in user settings), .gitignore for sensitive data, and isfs:// scheme for server-side browsing. Identical VS Code versions are not required, though using compatible extension versions is recommended. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/components/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GVSCO

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ISC_CPF_MERGE_FILE environment variable in a Docker Compose configuration for IRIS?

options.text: To specify a custom iris.cpf file that will completely replace the default configuration
To specify a CPF file containing configuration changes that will be merged with the default configuration
To enable automatic backup of the iris.cpf file
To specify the location where IRIS should write configuration changes

questions.explanation: ISC_CPF_MERGE_FILE specifies a CPF file containing configuration settings that will be merged into the default iris.cpf during container startup. This allows customizing specific settings (like memory, security, or namespaces) without maintaining a complete CPF file. The merge preserves default settings while applying your customizations. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ADOCK

questions.question: Which approach is recommended for monitoring the status and results of long-running background jobs started with the JOB command?

options.text: Use WAIT command to pause execution until the job completes
Implement a polling mechanism that checks a global or file for job status updates
Use RETURN values from the JOB command
Background jobs automatically send completion messages to the parent process

questions.explanation: Since background jobs run independently in separate processes, monitoring requires implementing a polling mechanism that checks persistent storage (globals, files, or database tables) for status updates. The background job writes status/progress to these locations, and monitoring code periodically checks them. There's no automatic notification mechanism. Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cjob
